Running Python code interactively: # I can see the certificate structure. The SubjectPublicKeyInfo is at:
# tbsCertificate.subjectPublicKeyInfo
# It has algorithm OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 (rsaEncryption) with NULL parameters

# I need to change this to 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10 (id-RSA-PSS) with malformed parameters
# Let me modify the DER encoding manually

# First, let me find the exact location of the algorithm OID in the DER
import struct

def find_sequence(data, target_offset=0):
    """Find all SEQUENCE boundaries in DER data"""
    results = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(data):
        if data[i] == 0x30:  # SEQUENCE
            if i + 1 < len(data):
                if data[i+1] & 0x80:  # Long form length
                    num_len_bytes = data[i+1] & 0x7f
                    length = 0
                    for j in range(num_len_bytes):
                        length = (length << 8) | data[i+2+j]
                    total = i + 2 + num_len_bytes + length
                else:
                    length = data[i+1]
                    total = i + 2 + length
                results.append((i, total, length))
                i = total
                continue
        i += 1
    return results

# Find the SPKI algorithm section
# The SPKI is: SEQUENCE { algorithm SEQUENCE { OID, NULL }, BIT STRING }
# Let me look at the raw bytes around the public key algorithm

cert_hex = cert_der.hex()
# Find "2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 01 01" (rsaEncryption OID: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1)
rsa_oid = bytes([0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01])
pos = cert_der.find(rsa_oid)
print(f"rsaEncryption OID found at position: {pos}")
print(f"Context bytes: {cert_der[pos-4:pos+20].hex()}")

# The structure around the OID should be:
# 30 <len> 06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 01 01 05 00
# SEQUENCE { OID(rsaEncryption), NULL }
# I need to change this to:
# 30 <len> 06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 01 0a <malformed_params>
# SEQUENCE { OID(id-RSA-PSS), <malformed_params> }

# The RSA-PSS OID is: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10
# DER encoding: 06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 01 0a
rsa_pss_oid = bytes([0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x0a])

# Let me look at the full structure around the SPKI
print(f"\nBytes around SPKI algorithm:")
print(f"Position {pos-10}: {cert_der[pos-10:pos+30].hex()}")
